mainTopic: Whether years can be added to a person's set lifespan; the end of פרק החולץ; and the new משנה on whether a second גט, מאמר, ביאה or חליצה takes effect
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the פסוק that promises a full lifespan. רבי עקיבא holds that a deserving person only gets to complete the years set for him, while the חכמים hold that years can even be added. The חכמים challenge רבי עקיבא from חזקיהו, who was promised fifteen extra years. רבי עקיבא answers that those years were his own, and supports this from the prophecy about יאשיהו, whose grandfather מנשה had not yet been born. The רבנן reject the proof, since the prophecy only says 'house of דוד.' Then רב יוסף remarks that the משנה's line about a wife or יבמה who died was not needed, and פרק החולץ ends. The new פרק opens with a מחלוקת between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים about whether a second גט, מאמר, ביאה or חליצה takes effect after a first one. The משנה then goes through cases of a יבם doing these acts in different orders, and ends with the rule that nothing works after חליצה or ביאה.

steps.title: Completing years versus adding years
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'the number of your days' as a person's set lifespan, and records an argument between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים about whether years can be added to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the years set for a person's life. רבי עקיבא says: if he deserves it, he is given all of his years; if not, years are taken away. The חכמים say: if he deserves it, years are added; if not, years are taken away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues explaining the פסוק 'I will fill the number of your days.' It says this means a person's set lifespan, and then lays out a מחלוקת about what happens to a deserving person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a person who does not deserve it loses years. They argue only about the deserving person. For רבי עקיבא he can at most reach his full set lifespan. For the חכמים he can even go past it.

keyTerms.meaning: The years of a person's life that were set for him before birth
He deserved it (through good deeds)
They complete: he gets all of his set years
They add: he gets years beyond what was set
They reduce: years are taken away

phrases.english: These are the years of the generations.
phrases.notes: This explains the פסוק 'את מספר ימיך אמלא' (שמות 23:26), meaning the lifespan set for each person.

phrases.english: If he is deserving, they complete his years;
if he is not deserving, they reduce his years;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say:
If he is deserving, they add to his years;
if he is not deserving, they reduce his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section, which explains the פסוק about filling a person's days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: a deserving person only completes his set lifespan. חכמים: a deserving person can receive years beyond it. Both agree years can be taken away.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי עקיבא from חזקיהו
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point to the פסוק where חזקיהו is told that fifteen years will be added to his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי עקיבא: but the פסוק says, 'I will add fifteen years to your days'!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי עקיבא's view using a פסוק that clearly says years were 'added' to someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said no one can live past his set years. The פסוק about חזקיהו uses the word 'add,' which sounds like years beyond what was set. That seems to support the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him: introduces a challenge from the other side
But the פסוק says
And I will add

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Akiva:
But it says:
"And I will add to your days fifteen years"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:5. This was said to King חזקיהו when he was sick and about to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's position from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that a deserving person only completes his set lifespan
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says years were 'added' to חזקיהו, which suggests living beyond the set lifespan.

steps.title: The added years were his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the fifteen years came out of חזקיהו's own original lifespan.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: they added to him from his own years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the challenge. The fifteen years were not extra; they were part of the years originally set for חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו was about to lose years. When those years were given back, the פסוק calls it 'adding' compared to the shortened life he was facing. So he never went past his original set lifespan.

keyTerms.meaning: From his own

phrases.english: He said to them:
From his own they added to him.
phrases.notes: He means the fifteen years were part of the lifespan originally set for him, which he was about to lose.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word 'add' in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Add' means years beyond a person's set lifespan.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Add' means giving back years from his own lifespan that were about to be taken away.

steps.title: Proof from the prophecy about יאשיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא proves his point: a prophet had already foretold that יאשיהו would be born, yet מנשה, the son of חזקיהו through whom יאשיהו would come, had not been born yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true: a prophet stood and prophesied, 'A son will be born to the house of דוד, יאשיהו is his name,' and מנשה had not yet been born!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא brings support for his answer. The prophecy about יאשיהו shows that חזקיהו was meant to live long enough to have מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיהו was to come from חזקיהו's line through מנשה. When חזקיהו lay sick, מנשה was not yet born. So חזקיהו's set lifespan must have included more years, and the fifteen years were his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so: introduces a supporting proof
Prophesies
יאשיהו, a later king of the house of דוד
מנשה, the son of חזקיהו

phrases.english: Know that this is so,
for a prophet stood and prophesied:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִנֵּה בֵן נוֹלָד לְבֵית דָּוִד יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ שְׁמוֹ״,
phrases.english: "Behold, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah is his name,"
and Manasseh had not yet been born!
phrases.notes: מנשה was חזקיהו's son and יאשיהו's grandfather, so חזקיהו still had to live long enough to father him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That חזקיהו's fifteen years were part of his own set lifespan
steps.raayaSupportSource: The prophecy in מלכים א 13:2 about יאשיהו, given before מנשה was born

steps.title: The רבנן: יאשיהו could come from someone else
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject the proof. The prophecy only says יאשיהו would come from the house of דוד, not specifically from חזקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Does it say 'from חזקיהו'? It says 'to the house of דוד.' He could be born from חזקיהו or from some other person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן would answer רבי עקיבא's proof. The prophecy does not name חזקיהו, so it proves nothing about his lifespan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's proof relied on the idea that יאשיהו had to come from חזקיהו. The רבנן point out that the פסוק only says 'house of דוד.' If חזקיהו had died, יאשיהו could have come from another descendant of דוד, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן: how do they answer?
Is it written...? A challenge meaning 'it doesn't say that'
A different person

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: you can only complete your set years, and חזקיהו's fifteen years were his own. חכמים: years can truly be added. The proof from יאשיהו is rejected because the prophecy only says 'house of דוד.'

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
Is it written "from Hezekiah"?
"To the house of David" is written;
he could be born either from Hezekiah,
or from another person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from יאשיהו, not רבי עקיבא's position itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed יאשיהו had to descend from חזקיהו, but the פסוק only says 'house of דוד.'

steps.title: רב יוסף: this line of the משנה was not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's cases of a wife or a יבמה who died, and רב יוסף says רבי taught a משנה that was not necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If his wife died...' 'If his יבמה died...' רב יוסף said: here רבי taught a משנה that was not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, quoting a line from our משנה about a man whose wife or יבמה died. רב יוסף remarks that this line teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that once the wife or יבמה has died, the man may marry her sister. רב יוסף holds this is already clear, since the תורה only forbids a wife's sister while the wife is alive. So this line did not need to be taught.

keyTerms.meaning: His יבמה: the widow of his brother who died childless
Etc.: the גמרא is quoting only the start of the line
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה
A משנה that was not needed because it adds nothing new

phrases.english: "His wife who died, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: if his wife died, he may marry her sister.

phrases.english: "His yevama who died, etc."
Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי מִשְׁנָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה.
phrases.english: Here Rabbi taught a mishna that is not necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁמֵּתָה וְכוּ׳ יְבִמְתּוֹ שֶׁמֵּתָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of lifespan and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף: the משנה's teaching that a man may marry the sister of his wife or יבמה after she died is unnecessary, since it adds nothing new.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק החולץ
steps.stepSummary: The formula that formally ends perek החולץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק החולץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the פרק called החולץ with the traditional closing line. No new argument is made here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך means 'we will return to you.' It marks the end of a פרק and expresses the hope to learn it again. The discussion that follows starts a brand-new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words said at the end of a perek
The name of the perek that is ending, taken from its first word

steps.whatToRemember: פרק החולץ, with its discussion of who counts as a ממזר and the story of רבי עקיבא and חזקיהו's years, is now finished.

phrases.english: We will return to you, perek HaCholetz

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole perek that steps 1-6 belonged to.

steps.title: Does a second act work after a first one?
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with a dispute. רבן גמליאל says no second גט, מאמר, ביאה or חליצה takes effect. The חכמים say a second גט and a second מאמר do take effect, but nothing works after ביאה or חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: there is no גט after a גט, no מאמר after a מאמר, no ביאה after a ביאה, and no חליצה after a חליצה. The חכמים say: there is a גט after a גט and a מאמר after a מאמר, but nothing works after ביאה or after חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a מחלוקת about a יבם who does an act toward a יבמה and then does the same kind of act again, either toward another יבמה or by another brother. They argue whether the second act counts at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that the first act settles the matter, so a repeat of the same act does nothing. The חכמים split the acts into two groups. A גט or a מאמר is a weaker act, so another one after it still has an effect. ביאה and חליצה are complete acts that end the יבום connection, so nothing done after them matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce. Here the יבם gives it to the יבמה to weaken the bond of יבום
Rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה by the יבם, with money or a document
Intercourse. For a יבמה, this is what makes יבום take effect
The ceremony that frees a יבמה from יבום
Anything at all

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'גט after גט' is not about one woman getting divorced twice in the ordinary way. It means a יבם gives a גט to one יבמה, and then a second גט is given, either to her צרה or by another brother. The question is whether that second גט does anything to the bond of יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the whole פרק. It shows the difference between weaker acts (גט, מאמר) and acts that close the case completely (ביאה, חליצה).

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
There is no bill of divorce after a bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: He means that once a גט was given to one יבמה, a second גט to her צרה, or from another brother, has no effect.

phrases.english: and no levirate betrothal after a levirate betrothal,
and no intercourse after intercourse,
and no chalitza after chalitza.
But the Sages say:
There is a bill of divorce after a bill of divorce,
and there is a levirate betrothal after a levirate betrothal.
But nothing works after intercourse,
and nothing at all works after chalitza.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֵין גֵּט אַחַר גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: no repeated act takes effect. חכמים: a repeated גט or מאמר does take effect, but nothing works after ביאה or חליצה.

steps.title: Cases that begin with מאמר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what happens when the יבם does a מאמר first and then gives a גט, does חליצה, or has ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he did a מאמר with his יבמה and then gave her a גט, she still needs חליצה from him. If he did a מאמר and then חליצה, she needs a גט from him. If he did a מאמר and then had ביאה, this is the proper way to do the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts walking through practical cases with one יבמה, all of them beginning with a מאמר. It shows what she still needs in each order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט after a מאמר undoes the מאמר but does not fully cut the bond of יבום, so she still needs חליצה. חליצה after a מאמר ends the bond of יבום, but the מאמר is a kind of betrothal, so a גט is needed to undo it. A מאמר followed by ביאה is the ideal way the חכמים set up for doing יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? This word introduces practical examples
His יבמה: his late brother's widow
She needs from him
According to its מצוה: the proper, ideal way

phrases.english: How so?
If he performed levirate betrothal with his yevama
and then gave her a bill of divorce,
she still needs chalitza from him.
If he performed levirate betrothal and then chalitza,
she needs a bill of divorce from him.
If he performed levirate betrothal and then had intercourse with her,
this is the proper way of the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical examples of how the acts listed in step 8 work together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מאמר then גט: she needs חליצה. מאמר then חליצה: she needs a גט. מאמר then ביאה: the ideal way.

steps.title: Cases that begin with a גט
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what happens when the יבם first gives a גט and then does a מאמר, has ביאה, or does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave a גט and then did a מאמר, she needs a גט and חליצה. If he gave a גט and then had ביאה, she needs a גט and חליצה. If he gave a גט and then did חליצה, nothing works after חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of cases, now starting with a גט. It shows that a גט does not end the bond of יבום, but חליצה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a גט she is forbidden to him, so a later מאמר or ביאה cannot finish the יבום. Each of them only creates a betrothal that needs another גט, and the bond of יבום still needs חליצה. Once חליצה is done the bond is fully gone, so the order of acts before it does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave a bill of divorce
And he performed חליצה
And he had intercourse with her

steps.whatToRemember: A גט or a מאמר only weakens or changes the bond of יבום. חליצה (and ביאה done in the proper way) ends it completely, so 'nothing works after חליצה.'

phrases.english: If he gave a bill of divorce and then performed levirate betrothal,
she needs a bill of divorce and chalitza.
If he gave a bill of divorce and then had intercourse with her,
she needs a bill of divorce and chalitza.
If he gave a bill of divorce and then performed chalitza,
nothing works after chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases from step 9, now starting with a גט instead of a מאמר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גט then מאמר or ביאה: she needs a גט and חליצה. גט then חליצה: nothing works after חליצה.

steps.title: Nothing done after חליצה takes effect
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two more groups of cases. In the first, the יבם does חליצה and afterward does either a מאמר, a גט, or ביאה. In the second, he has ביאה and afterward does either a מאמר, a גט, or חליצה. In all of them, nothing done afterward takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did חליצה and then did a מאמר, or gave a גט, or had relations; or if he had relations and then did a מאמר, or gave a גט, or did חליצה, nothing done after חליצה (or after ביאה) has any effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of orders by looking at cases where חליצה is part of the sequence. Its ruling is that once חליצה is done, any act after it means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 and 10 covered orders that started with a מאמר or a גט. Now the משנה deals with orders that start with חליצה or with ביאה. This matches the חכמים in step 8, who said nothing works after ביאה or חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He performed חליצה, the release ceremony that frees the יבמה from the יבם
He had relations with her (ביאה), which is the full act of יבום
After
Anything; here it means nothing takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: חליצה is a final stop. After it, a מאמר, a גט, or even ביאה does nothing, because the bond with the יבם is already finished.
steps.confusionAlert: The closing words mention only חליצה, but in the second order ביאה came first. The rule from step 8 still applies: the חכמים said nothing works after ביאה either. Do not read this line as saying that the acts after ביאה do take effect.

phrases.english: If he performed the release ceremony and then did a betrothal-statement,
or gave a bill of divorce, or had relations,
or if he had relations and then did a betrothal-statement,
or gave a bill of divorce, or performed the release ceremony —
after the release ceremony, nothing takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of orders. After the מאמר-first order (step 9) and the גט-first order (step 10), it now gives the orders that start with חליצה or with ביאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once חליצה or ביאה has been done, any later מאמר, גט, ביאה or חליצה has no effect on the bond of יבום. This matches the חכמים in step 8: nothing works after ביאה or after חליצה.
